_meta.title: Celerey Backend Specification
_meta.description: Full backend requirements covering: (1) subscription/entitlement system for free-trial gating, (2) missing or misaligned API fields discovered by frontend audit, (3) risk assessment scoring engine with full endpoint spec.

section_1_subscription_and_entitlements.overview: The frontend uses a localStorage-based subscription status ('none' | 'trialing' | 'active') set at login. This must be replaced or supplemented by a server-authoritative entitlement object returned from the API so limitations cannot be bypassed client-side.

required_user_object_additions.description: The following fields must be added to the user object returned by user.get and user.update so the frontend can enforce limits without a separate round-trip.

subscription_status.description: Current subscription state. 'none' = no plan, 'trialing' = free trial, 'active' = paid subscriber.

subscription_plan.description: The named plan tier. Null when subscription_status is 'none'.

trial_started_at.description: Timestamp when the trial began. Used by frontend to show trial countdown.

is_enterprise.description: True if user is on an enterprise plan. Enterprise users bypass all feature limits.

entitlements.description: Server-authoritative feature flags. Frontend checks these before allowing actions. All false for free trial unless specified.

insights_full.description: Access to all AI insights cards (free trial: only first 2 visible).

advisor_chat.description: Access to the advisor page and messaging.

concierge_requests.description: Ability to submit concierge service requests.

live_market_data.description: Live price refresh on assets page.

portfolio_charts.description: Portfolio performance area chart on assets page.

cash_flow_projections.description: Forward-projected (dashed) lines on the cash flow chart.

record_limits.description: Maximum records a user may create per entity. Null means unlimited (paid plans). Backend must enforce these limits and return 403 with code RECORD_LIMIT_REACHED if exceeded.

backend_enforcement_rules.description: These rules must be enforced server-side. Frontend gating is UX only — the API is the source of truth.

rules.behavior: Before inserting, count existing active records for the user. If count >= limit for their plan, return HTTP 403 with body: { error: true, code: 'RECORD_LIMIT_REACHED', entity: 'goals', limit: 3, current: 3 }
Return HTTP 403 with body: { error: true, code: 'FEATURE_NOT_ENTITLED', feature: 'advisor_chat' }
When trial_ends_at has passed and subscription_status has not been upgraded, set subscription_status to 'none' automatically. All entitlements should reflect this.

new_endpoints.description: Returns the current user's full entitlement state. Frontend calls this on dashboard load to hydrate the store.
Initiates a plan upgrade. Integrate with payment provider. On success, update subscription_status to 'active' and unlock entitlements.

section_2_missing_and_misaligned_api_fie.overview: Audit of what the frontend displays or sends that the current API does not return or accept. Each item identifies the API operation, what is missing, and what needs to be added.

missing_fields.issue: The frontend sends and expects description on every goal create/update and displays it on the goal card. The API interface has the field typed as optional (description?: string) but it is not confirmed to be persisted or returned by goals.find. Must be stored and returned.
missing_fields.action: Ensure description is a persisted column on the goals table and included in all find/create/update responses.

missing_fields.issue: The frontend mapper defaults category to 'other' because goals.find does not return it. It is sent on create but not round-tripped. Goal cards use category for icon selection.
missing_fields.action: Add category as a persisted column and return it in all goal responses.

missing_fields.issue: Frontend sends icon on create for display purposes but it is not confirmed returned on find.
missing_fields.action: Persist and return icon.

missing_fields.issue: Same as icon — sent on create but not confirmed returned.
missing_fields.action: Persist and return color.

missing_fields.issue: The API returns amount_monthly on find but the create/update payload uses amount. The frontend mapper handles both but this is fragile. Standardise on a single field name.
missing_fields.action: Standardise response field to amount_monthly on all income responses, or return both.

missing_fields.issue: Find returns is_recurring (boolean) but create/update accepts recurring_type (string: 'monthly', 'one-time'). Frontend maps both but behaviour diverges.
missing_fields.action: Return recurring_type on all income find responses so round-trips are lossless.

missing_fields.issue: The CashFlowEntryDraft type in the frontend includes a note field shown in the UI, but it is not sent to or returned from the API.
missing_fields.action: Add note as an optional persisted column on income records.

missing_fields.issue: Same inconsistency as income — see above.
missing_fields.action: Standardise to amount_monthly in responses.

missing_fields.issue: Same as income. recurring_type must be returned in find.
missing_fields.action: Return recurring_type on all expense find responses.

missing_fields.issue: Same as income — note is shown in the UI form but not persisted.
missing_fields.action: Add note as optional persisted column on expense records.

missing_fields.issue: The API sometimes returns amount instead of balance. The frontend mapper handles both but this should be standardised.
missing_fields.action: Always return balance in liability responses.

missing_fields.issue: Sent on create but the casing is camelCase which is unusual for a REST API. Confirm the API accepts and returns this field by this exact name or document the snake_case equivalent.
missing_fields.action: Document and standardise: either interest_rate_pct (snake_case) or confirm camelCase is intentional.

missing_fields.issue: Same casing issue as interestRatePct.
missing_fields.action: Standardise to min_payment_monthly in API responses and update frontend mapper.

missing_fields.issue: Displayed in the UI (due date of monthly payment). Mapper reads l.dueDay but API likely uses due_day.
missing_fields.action: Return due_day (snake_case) and update frontend mapper.

missing_fields.issue: The frontend fetches live prices from a third-party cache (asset_live_prices_v1 in localStorage) but there is no backend endpoint to serve or cache live market data. This means prices go stale across devices.
missing_fields.action: Add GET /api/v1/assets/prices?symbols=AAPL,TSLA that returns latest prices. Cache server-side for 2 hours.

missing_fields.issue: The assets page shows a portfolio performance chart (area chart) but there is no endpoint to fetch historical valuations per holding.
missing_fields.action: Add GET /api/v1/assets/:holding_id/valuations returning array of { as_of, value } sorted ascending.

missing_fields.issue: Frontend defaults this to 85 since the API does not store it. It is shown as an editable field in the retirement UI.
missing_fields.action: Add life_expectancy as a persisted field on the retirement record.

missing_fields.issue: Frontend defaults to 7%. Shown as editable slider in retirement what-if tool.
missing_fields.action: Add expected_return_pct to retirement record.

missing_fields.issue: Frontend defaults to 2%. Same as above.
missing_fields.action: Add inflation_pct to retirement record.

missing_fields.issue: Frontend defaults to 4%. Shown in retirement summary and used in calculations.
missing_fields.action: Add safe_withdrawal_rate_pct to retirement record.

missing_endpoints.description: Fetch the current user's retirement configuration. Already called as retirement.find in bootstrap but not confirmed to exist as a standalone endpoint.
missing_endpoints.action: Confirm this endpoint exists and returns all fields above.

missing_endpoints.description: Update retirement configuration. Currently called as retirement.update in the frontend but not confirmed to exist.

missing_fields.issue: The user object has risk_profile typed but the risk assessment is currently stored only in localStorage (key: risk_attitude_result_v1). This means it is lost on device change and cannot be used server-side for recommendations.
missing_fields.action: When a risk assessment is submitted (see Section 3), update risk_profile on the user record with the result band string. Return it in user.get.

missing_fields.issue: Already in the API schema but used as a modifier in risk scoring. Confirm it is persisted as a number (count) not a string or array.
missing_fields.action: Confirm dependents is stored and returned as an integer representing count.

missing_fields.issue: Used as a risk scoring modifier (see Section 3) but not currently on the user record or any API response. Must be derived or stored.
missing_fields.action: Add debt_level as a computed or user-supplied field. Can be computed by the backend from total liabilities vs income, or collected during profile setup. Required for risk scoring.

missing_fields.issue: The ApiHistoryPoint interface shows surplus as optional. The frontend uses it for the cash flow chart tooltip. If the backend does not compute and return it, the frontend falls back to income - expenses which may differ due to rounding.
missing_fields.action: Always compute and return surplus in history records as income - expenses.

missing_endpoints.description: Submit a concierge service inquiry. Currently the frontend logs the payload to console only — there is no API call being made. Must be gated by the concierge_requests entitlement.

request_body.notes: I would like to discuss rebalancing my equity portfolio.

missing_endpoints.description: List all inquiries submitted by the current user.
Returns the assigned advisor details for the current user. Currently uses static mock data (advisorData in client-data.ts).

response_example.name: Sarah Williams
response_example.title: Certified Financial Planner
response_example.bio: 15 years experience in personal wealth management.

missing_endpoints.description: Returns personalised action items generated by the advisor or AI. Currently uses static mock data.
Submit a new advisor meeting or question request. Gated by advisor_chat entitlement.

request_body.notes: I want to review my retirement allocation.

missing_endpoints.description: Submit a support ticket from the Support page. Currently only logs to console.

request_body.subject: Question about my invoice
request_body.message: I was charged twice this month.

missing_endpoints.description: Trigger a data export. Returns a JSON file of all user financial data. Gated by export_data entitlement.

section_3_risk_assessment_engine.overview: Full specification for the risk scoring engine. Currently the frontend calculates scores locally and stores results in localStorage only. The backend must implement the scoring engine authoritatively, persist assessments, and expose the endpoints below.

questions.question: What is your primary investment objective?

options.label: Preserving my capital and avoiding losses

questions.question: If your investment portfolio declined by 20% in a year, what would you most likely do?

options.label: Sell part of the portfolio to reduce risk
Hold the investments and wait for recovery
Review and rebalance but stay invested
Invest additional money at lower prices

questions.note: Q3 and Q10 are averaged before scoring. The combined time_horizon_factor carries 17% weight (0.12 + 0.05).
questions.question: How long do you plan to keep the majority of your investments before needing the funds?
How experienced are you with investing?
How comfortable are you with investment volatility?

options.label: I am comfortable with significant fluctuations
I accept high volatility for higher returns

questions.question: How much of your total savings are you planning to invest this year?
If markets fell by 30% during a financial crisis, what would you most likely do?

options.label: Sell everything to avoid further losses
Review and rebalance but remain invested

questions.question: How stable is your primary source of income?

options.label: Government or long term secure employment

questions.question: Do you currently hold investments across multiple asset classes?

questions.note: Averaged with Q3 before scoring to eliminate double-counting of time horizon.
questions.question: When will you likely need access to a significant portion of this investment?

step_1_time_horizon_preprocessing.description: Before running the weighted formula, average Q3 and Q10 into a single time_horizon_factor to eliminate redundancy.

step_2_weighted_questionnaire_score.description: Apply weights to each question. Q3 and Q10 are replaced by time_horizon_factor.

step_3_profile_modifiers.description: Additive adjustments based on profile-level data collected at onboarding. Applied after questionnaire score.

debt_modifier.source: user.debt_level (low | medium | high) — see Section 2 user_profile

step_4_final_score.formula: final_score = clamp(questionnaire_score + age_mod + dependents_mod + debt_mod + emergency_fund_mod, 1.0, 5.0)

bands.description: You prioritize protecting your capital above all else, preferring stable and predictable returns over growth.
bands.strategy: Capital preservation instruments: T-bills, money market funds, fixed deposits.

bands.description: You prefer lower-risk investments and can tolerate only small fluctuations in pursuit of modest returns.
You are comfortable with a balanced approach, accepting moderate volatility for a mix of growth and income.
You are focused on long-term capital growth and comfortable with significant market fluctuations.
You accept high volatility and significant short-term losses in pursuit of maximum long-term capital growth.
bands.strategy: High-growth strategy with higher-risk asset exposure.

submission_payload.description: POST body sent by frontend when user completes the questionnaire.

result.description: You are comfortable with a balanced approach, accepting moderate volatility for a mix of growth and income.

endpoints.description: Submit questionnaire answers. Backend runs the full scoring engine (questionnaire + profile modifiers). Returns the result immediately and persists it. Also updates risk_profile on the user record.
side_effects: Updates user.risk_profile with the result band string

endpoints.description: Retrieve a specific assessment by ID. Returns full scoring breakdown.
Return all past assessments for a user, sorted newest first. Used to show retake history.
Shortcut to return the most recent assessment for the authenticated user. Used by the dashboard on load.
Return the active question set with options and score mappings. Allows frontend to render the questionnaire dynamically from API rather than hardcoded.

response_example.questions: [ ... array of question objects as defined in questionnaire section above ... ]

endpoints.description: Update profile-level modifiers independently of questionnaire answers. Used when a user adds a dependent, pays off debt, or hits a birthday milestone. Does NOT create a new assessment — use /recalculate for that.

Re-run the scoring engine using the stored questionnaire responses from the latest assessment but with the latest profile data. Creates a new assessment record (does not overwrite the old one) and links it as a re-score event. Returns the new assessment.

POST /risk/submit: Each response must be an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive
Score 4 is valid for q2 and q7 — do not reject it
questionnaire_version must match the active version stored in the system
Profile modifiers: age must be a positive integer >= 18
debt_level must be one of: low, medium, high
emergency_fund_status must be one of: none, partial, full
country_code must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code

error_response_standard.description: All risk endpoints must return errors in this format.

versioning_notes: Store questionnaire_version on every assessment record.
If the question set changes, old assessments remain valid under their original version and must not be retroactively rescored unless explicitly triggered via /recalculate.
Take a profile_snapshot at the time of scoring and store it on the assessment record so historical assessments reflect the data used at that time.
